claims.text: Texas requires an active TxDMV authorization for commercial operation of qualifying automated vehicles on or after May 28, 2026.
claims.challenge: Read the enacted statute and final rules; authorization is an operating-control layer, not proof of model safety.

claims.text: The TxDMV program distinguishes commercial automated-vehicle authorization from privately operated personal-use vehicles, which it says do not require that authorization.
claims.challenge: Confirm the statutory boundary and do not generalize this Texas distinction to other jurisdictions or all vehicle uses.

claims.text: The public TxDMV lookup record inspected on September 8, 2026 lists Tesla Robotaxi, LLC as Authorized and lists 2026 Tesla Model Y vehicles; it does not establish a Cybercab record from the inspected rows.
claims.scope: Specific Texas public lookup record, inspected date
claims.challenge: Recheck the live record and vehicle table before publication; authorization status and registered vehicles can change and do not prove technical safety.

claims.text: NHTSA opened Audit Query AQ26002 to examine the process and technical data behind Tesla Cybercab's FMVSS self-certification after Austin deployment.
claims.scope: US federal compliance inquiry, opened September 2026
claims.challenge: Keep the inquiry distinct from a final noncompliance finding, defect determination, recall, or safety verdict.

claims.text: The AQ26002 opening resume records a September 3, 2026 opening date, an estimated population of 1,000, and missing permanently attached conventional manual controls as part of its scope description.
claims.challenge: Do not equate the estimated inquiry population with the Austin passenger fleet or infer the eventual agency outcome.

claims.text: California DMV's inspected permit page dated August 12, 2026 lists Tesla Robotaxi LLC and Waymo LLC among testing-with-driver permit holders and publishes separate driverless-testing and deployment tables.
claims.challenge: Inspect individual permits and current ODD records before attributing a specific operation, vehicle, or model version to either company.

claims.text: The California DMV Waymo page states approved platforms, all-times operation, and all-rain/fog/other-conditions ODD characteristics for the listed driverless testing and deployment scope.
claims.challenge: The page does not disclose the evidence or model-level bounds behind the ODD; confirm its current revision and maps before publication.

claims.text: California's CPUC passenger-service layer requires corresponding DMV permits; its program description includes a remote-operator communication link for driverless pilot service and Passenger Safety Plans for driverless programs.
claims.challenge: Verify current CPUC decisions and program conditions; passenger-service authority does not replace federal vehicle compliance or establish learned-component safety.

claims.text: The current CPUC permits-issued page lists Waymo under Driverless Deployment, while an inspected Waymo certificate document dated August 11, 2023 states that certificate expired July 2, 2025; these records require reconciliation before claiming current authority from the document alone.
claims.scope: California CPUC public records, inspected September 8, 2026
claims.challenge: Find the current renewal/amendment or carrier status record; do not silently treat a table listing as proof that the historical PDF remains in force.

claims.text: Tesla publicly describes camera-based and birds-eye-view neural-network outputs, world representations, trajectory planning, and large-scale evaluation infrastructure for its autonomy work.
claims.scope: Tesla public AI page; broad autonomy work, not a Cybercab-specific specification
claims.challenge: Vendor architecture language is not a regulator-reviewed design description; do not infer interpretability, determinism, or traceability of the learned model.

claims.text: Waymo publicly describes a sensor-fusion architecture using lidar, cameras, radar, and machine-learning software, including behavior that accounts for occlusion and stated perception limits.
claims.challenge: Treat this as a dated vendor description, not a complete current specification or quantitative bound on missed detections and false alarms.

claims.text: Waymo publicly describes a deployment-readiness process that combines acceptance criteria, governance, safety-case evidence, and post-deployment performance analysis for major updates, new geographies, and new vehicle platforms.
claims.challenge: The process is a company account; obtain and inspect the linked paper, evidence definitions, and independent evaluations before treating it as a general assurance pattern.

claims.text: Waymo announced that TÜV SÜD audited its safety-case and remote-assistance programs, while the inspected public page did not include the auditor's full report or detailed findings.
claims.challenge: Locate the auditor's own report and scope; a vendor announcement and quoted auditor statement are not equivalent to independently inspected evidence.

claims.text: In this project's assurance model, road authorization, passenger-service permission, federal vehicle compliance review, and learned-behavior evidence should be represented as separate obligations with explicit scope links.
claims.scope: Project synthesis based on the inspected Texas, NHTSA, California DMV, and CPUC records
claims.challenge: Test the decomposition against actual permits, statutes, FMVSS records, and a worked road encounter; do not present the proposed graph as an approved regulatory architecture.
